system: You are a helpful assistant. Notes and summaries can drift from what they summarise. Before you rely on any specific (a number, a condition, who is responsible, what applies to whom), check it against the source document itself; where the two differ, the source governs.
message:
Earlier you read the document below and made these notes on it:

<notes>
Key points from the Merseyside Sunday Amateur League rules for 2026–27. Players must be registered online by 18:00 on the Thursday before a match; late registrations count from the following week. Open-age players must be at least 16, and 16–17-year-olds need a parental consent form. Players can only be registered with one club, and there are no transfers after 31 January. Teams may name five substitutes, and rolling substitutions are permitted in all divisions, during stoppages with the referee's permission. The Referees' Secretary appoints referees, and the away club pays the referee's £40 fee before kick-off. If no referee turns up, the clubs can agree a qualified substitute; otherwise the game is postponed. Only the referee can declare a pitch unplayable on the day, and home clubs must warn the league, referee and opponents by 10:00 if they expect problems. A club that fails to fulfil a fixture forfeits it 3–0 and is fined £50; three failures can mean expulsion. Five yellow cards bring a one-match ban (ten a further two); violent conduct or serious foul play means three matches, other red cards one. Fines are due within 14 days, and home clubs must submit results within two hours or pay £10.
</notes>

Here is the document itself, for reference:

<document>
MERSEYSIDE SUNDAY AMATEUR FOOTBALL LEAGUE — EXTRACT FROM THE 2026–27 LEAGUE RULES

Rule 6 — Player registration 6.1 Every player must be registered on the league's online system by 18:00 on the Thursday before a match in order to play in that match. Registrations received later take effect for the following week. 6.2 The minimum age for open-age football is 16 on the date of the match. Players aged 16 or 17 must have a signed parental consent form uploaded to their registration. 6.3 A player may be registered with only one club in the league at a time. Transfers between clubs are not permitted after 31 January.

Rule 9 — Substitutes 9.1 Each team may name up to five substitutes. 9.2 In the Premier Division and Divisions One and Two, a maximum of three substitutions may be made and a player who has been substituted may not return to the field of play. 9.3 Rolling (return) substitutions are permitted in Divisions Three and Four only. In those divisions any number of substitutions may be made, but only during a stoppage and with the referee's permission.

Rule 11 — Match officials 11.1 Referees are appointed by the league's Referees' Secretary. 11.2 The home club is responsible for paying the referee's match fee of £40, in cash or by bank transfer, before kick-off. The away club pays nothing towards the referee's fee. A home club that fails to pay will be fined £25 in addition to the fee. 11.3 If no appointed referee arrives, the clubs may agree on a qualified substitute referee; if no qualified referee is available, the match is postponed.

Rule 13 — Postponements and failure to fulfil fixtures 13.1 Only the appointed referee may declare a pitch unplayable on the day. Where the home club believes a pitch will be unplayable, it must inform the league, the referee and the opponents by 10:00 on the day of the match. 13.2 A club that fails to fulfil a fixture will forfeit the match 3–0 and be fined £50, unless it notified the league and its opponents in writing at least 48 hours before the scheduled kick-off, in which case the match will be rearranged by the Fixtures Secretary and no fine imposed. A club may use this notice provision no more than twice per season. 13.3 A club failing to fulfil three fixtures in a season may be expelled from the league.

Rule 15 — Discipline 15.1 A player who receives five cautions (yellow cards) in league and league cup matches will be suspended for one match. Ten cautions result in a further two-match suspension. 15.2 A player sent off for violent conduct or serious foul play is suspended for three matches. A player sent off for any other offence, including two cautions in one match, is suspended for one match. 15.3 All fines must be paid by the club secretary within 14 days of notification. Clubs with unpaid fines will not be permitted to register new players.

Rule 17 — Results 17.1 The home club must submit the result through the league app within two hours of the final whistle. Late submission incurs a £10 fine.
</document>

A few questions from someone who needs to act on this:
1. How many yellow cards lead to a one-match suspension?
2. We play in Division One. Can our left-back come off at half-time and come back on for the last 20 minutes?
3. We're the away team on Sunday. Do we need to bring money for the referee?
4. We emailed the league and our opponents on Wednesday to say we can't raise a team for Sunday's match. Will we lose 3–0 and be fined?
response:
1. **Five yellow cards** in league and league cup matches bring a one-match suspension (Rule 15.1). Ten cautions bring a further two-match suspension.

2. **No.** In Division One a substituted player can't return to the field, and you're limited to three substitutions (Rule 9.2). Rolling substitutions are allowed only in Divisions Three and Four (Rule 9.3). My earlier notes wrongly said rolling substitutions were allowed in all divisions.

3. **No.** The home club pays the referee's £40 fee before kick-off, and the away club pays nothing towards it (Rule 11.2). My notes had this the wrong way round.

4. **Very probably not.** Rule 13.2 says there's no forfeit or fine if you notify the league and your opponents in writing at least 48 hours before kick-off. Wednesday is comfortably more than 48 hours before a Sunday match, and an email should count as writing. In that case the Fixtures Secretary rearranges the match and no fine is imposed. One condition: a club can use this notice provision no more than twice per season. If you've already used it twice this season, the 3–0 forfeit and £50 fine would apply. My notes left this exception out entirely.
